court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Shri Balkrishna Pandurang Halde And ... vs Smt. Yeshodabai Balkrishna Halde

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Balkrishna Pandurang Halde, Jankabai Popat Vatphade @ Jankabai Pandurang Halde, Pradip Balkrishna Halde, Nilesh Balkrishna Halde (husband, wife, children)
parties.respondent_defendant: Yeshodabai Balkrishna Halde, Jyoti Sahebrao Pawar, Varsha Shantaram Handore (wife, household, household)

facts_of_case: Unsuccessful Defendants against the 'Common Judgment and Decree' dated 4th September 2013 passed by District Judge-1, Niphad, District Nashik. Suit was filed for partition and separate possession of their 1/4th share each in the suit properties.

legal_principles.principle: A decree passed in a judicial proceeding is conclusive evidence of the title to the property.
legal_principles.held: As observed by the first Appellate Court, there is nothing on record to show that the said Judgment is challenged by Appellant No.1 or it is reversed or set aside.

legal_principles.principle: A person's bare and interested words are not sufficient to prove a fact, especially when there is no supporting evidence.
legal_principles.held: She has also not produced any documentary evidence, like the Cheque, Pass- Book, Bank Statement or recitals in the 'Sale-Deed'.

legal_principles.principle: A person who inherits ancestral joint family properties is entitled to their share in those properties.
legal_principles.held: In his cross-examination also, Appellant No.1 has admitted the fact that he has received these properties in the partition.

outcome.final_order: Both Second Appeals are preferred by the unsuccessful Defendants against the 'Common Judgment and Decree' dated 4th September 2013 passed by District Judge-1, Niphad, District Nashik.

use_for_drafting: advising on property division in joint families
